why: compared the artifact's float32 dense vector byte-for-byte against
what the target returned. Against aw_e8 (dense datatype float16)
that can never match: 0 of 14,819 rows compared identical after a
write that was otherwise correct (task 598 SS4).
These pairs are REAL: the artifact side is the task-598 pack row
projected through the applier's own write path (upsert_wave_prod.
to_point), the stored side is what the live twin returned for the
same id after that write. They are the evidence that the dense leg
-- and ONLY the dense leg -- is rounded by float16 storage: the
bm25 sparse values come back bit-identical (the SparseIndexParams
datatype governs the index, not the stored value), so the sparse
and payload halves of the comparison stay byte-exact.
